description: Golden payroll Phase 11: first-cutoff money-waterfall, employer/agency loans, voluntary Pag-IBIG, loan balance bounds, refusal states and exact-centavo posting/replay helpers; expected monetary values are hand-derived, not copied from calculation output.

sources.statutory: Same 2026 first-cutoff assumptions and published Philippine SSS, PhilHealth, Pag-IBIG and BIR semi-monthly rules as golden phases 6 and 8; mandatory contributions precede voluntary/loan deductions.
sources.loan: Current PayrollPH source: src/lib/payroll-engine.ts (government-loan priority, active/effective loan filters and disposable-pay limits); src/lib/payroll-loan-approval.ts (schedule validation); src/lib/payroll-loan-settlement.ts (exact settlement and replay). Certification of current source behavior is not legal permission for payroll deduction.
sources.voluntary: Current PayrollPH source: employee.pagIbigVoluntaryMonthly, split first cutoff; voluntary deductions do not reduce BIR taxable compensation.

assumptions: All engine-backed payroll cases use the September 1-15, 2026 first cutoff, an active monthly-salaried fictional employee, split statutory timing and no attendance exceptions or holidays.
PHP 30,000 monthly: gross 15,000, SSS 750, PhilHealth 375, mandatory Pag-IBIG 100, taxable 13,775, withholding 503.70, net before optional deductions 13,271.30.
PHP 10,000 monthly: gross 5,000, SSS 250, PhilHealth 125, mandatory Pag-IBIG 100, withholding zero, disposable pay 4,525 before optional deductions.

Only active loans effective during the cutoff are considered. A loan can deduct no more than the lesser of its scheduled cutoff and unpaid balance; government loans precede company loans; elective deductions cannot make net negative.
Fixture active loans have no real lender or employee consent. No release, loan-payment posting, remittance or legal wage-deduction authorization is performed.

baseline.description: No optional deductions; statutory and tax components form the invariant baseline.

activeCompany.description: An active company loan with 600.00 scheduled deducts exactly 600.00 after mandatory items; taxable pay and WHT remain fixed.

activeSss.description: SSS salary loan amortization of 375.25 is centavo-exact and is not another statutory contribution.

lastInstallmentCapped.description: Scheduled 600.00 against a 125.25 unpaid balance is capped to the 125.25 remaining, not the full installment.

pendingIgnored.description: A pending-approval company loan cannot reduce take-home pay.

pausedAndPaidIgnored.description: Paused and paid-off agency/company loans are both absent from the calculation.

futureAndExpiredIgnored.description: A future-start loan and an already-ended loan are ineligible at the September cutoff.

inclusiveDateBoundary.description: September 15 loan start and September 1 loan end still overlap the actual cutoff, so each 100.00 installment applies.

voluntaryBeforeLoans.description: PHP 400 monthly voluntary Pag-IBIG uses PHP 200 in split first cutoff without lowering taxable compensation or WHT.

mixedAgencyCompanyVoluntary.description: Voluntary 200 and SSS 300 plus company 500 all fit in 13,271.30, giving 1,000.00 extra deductions.

governmentBeforeCompanyShortfall.description: Company loan is inserted first, but SSS must receive 4,000.00 of the 4,025.00 remaining after mandatory 475 and voluntary 500, leaving exactly 25.00 to company and zero net.

invalidZeroInstallment.description: Active legacy loan with zero scheduled deduction is excluded and raises a fail-closed reconciliation exception, never a wage credit.

activeZeroBalanceIgnored.description: Active legacy row with a paid-off zero balance is not amortized.

limitations: This certifies deterministic calculations against fictional disposable PostgreSQL only, not authorized real salary deductions or employer payroll release.
The engine's loan balances are read-only until release; Phase 11 tests exact-centavo settlement helpers separately, not the end-to-end release and repayment ledger.

Company/agency loan authorization evidence, lawful consent, remittance handling, over-collection disputes, benefits enrollment, wage advances and year-end/final-pay interactions are not certified here.
Only monthly-salaried first cutoffs are exercised; second-cutoff true-up, daily/hourly, attendance, other earning/benefit sources and statutory changes are outside this phase.
Sources and expected values need independent Philippine payroll/legal practitioner review before any filing, withholding, loan collection or production use.
